rationale: A legitimate cross-family pairing of the archive's best slope leg (gross margin) with its best alpha leg (wcap/lt) using the MIN combiner that has repeatedly worked here, with no shared variables and a coherent complementarity story, though it remains an incremental leg swap within an already well-mined family.

Netting cash out of the load leg is economically defensible and materially reorders cash-rich levered firms rather than rescaling them, but it is a modest refinement of the archived leader whose incremental information over gross liabilities is likely small since che is typically a minor fraction of lt.

The financial-versus-operating-claims decomposition is the single most defensible remaining variation on the leader's load leg and yields an interpretable three-way comparison, but like Signal 2 it is a one-variable substitution within an already-tested construct rather than a new mechanism.

The ingredients (earnings-stream volatility × leverage) replicate the economics of the archived CashFlowVolatilityLeverageDefaultProxy and sit close to the published earnings-volatility/distress-risk anomalies, so only the combiner and the scaling denominator are genuinely new; the change is more than cosmetic but the incremental hypothesis content is thin.

The expression algebraically reduces to gross margin minus lt/revt, and since gross margin is bounded in [0,1] while lt/revt is unbounded and far more dispersed, the composite is dominated by the leverage-to-sales leg — so it does not test the claimed "balanced pooling" and largely reduces to a single known leverage ratio.

The construct is internally inconsistent with its negative expected sign: MIN(RANK(margin), RANK(load)) is monotonically increasing in gross margin, a leg the archive shows predicts returns positively, and its low tail pools genuinely safe low-load firms with genuinely weak low-margin firms, so both tails are muddled and the direction is unidentified — the same defect that produced ProfitableButIlliquid's wrong-signed slope.
